notes: Supported sources for 9.1: vSphere 8.x (with Aria Operations 8.x, optionally NSX 4.x and Aria Automation 8.x) and VCF 5.x.
vSphere 8.x reaches end of support in October 2027.
Baseline-managed (VUM) clusters are not supported in vSphere 9. Host Profiles are deprecated.
Licensing moves from 25-character keys to subscription licence files.
VVF 9.1 uses the same ESX 9.x CPU and hardware rules as VCF 9.1.
VVF has a smaller entitlement than VCF. Confirm whether NSX, VCF Automation and other selected features are included in the VVF subscription before planning them.

vSAN: Confirm each host model, NIC, storage controller and disk firmware on the vSAN HCL for the target release.
Clear any resync or health alarms before starting.
Check whether the cluster is OSA or ESA and plan the disk format upgrade separately.
NSX: NSX 4.x is a supported source for the VCF 9.1 upgrade path. NSX for vSphere (NSX-V) has no direct path and needs migrating first.
Check Edge and Transport Node hardware and NIC support.
Plan the NSX upgrade order against the vCenter and ESX order in the Broadcom upgrade sequence KB.
VCF Operations: Aria Operations 8.x is a supported source for the 9.1 path. Confirm the exact 8.x build.
Plan for VCF Operations fleet management and the new licensing model.
VCF Automation: Aria Automation 8.x has a supported source path to 9.1. Confirm the exact 8.x build and any custom content.
Inventory blueprints, extensibility and integrations before starting.
vSphere Kubernetes Service: Check Supervisor and workload cluster versions against the Broadcom interoperability matrix for the target.
Confirm load balancer and networking choice (NSX or VDS with external LB).

manualChecks: RVTools does not show lifecycle method. Confirm every cluster uses vSphere Lifecycle Manager images, not baselines (VUM baselines are not supported in vSphere 9).
RVTools does not show Host Profile use. Host Profiles are deprecated in VCF 9.0. Plan a move to vSphere Configuration Profiles.
If the source is VCF 5.x, upgrade via SDDC Manager on the supported path rather than treating it as plain vSphere.
Check third-party products (backup, monitoring, storage plugins, security agents) for support on vSphere 9.
Check the exact HBA, NIC and firmware combinations for every host model. RVTools does not capture firmware.
Confirm licence files for the target subscription before any upgrade window.
